record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.original_question: Does there exist a zero-dimensional space X that is not countable dense homogeneous while its square X^2 is countable dense homogeneous, and can such an X be chosen to be rigid?

evidence.quote: Problem 17 (Medini [58]). Is there a zero-dimensional space X that is not CDH while X2 is CDH? Can X be rigid?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A separable topological space $X$ is called countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D, E \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h : X \to X$ with $h(D) = E$. The space $X$ is called rigid if the only homeomorphism from $X$ onto itself is the identity. The space $X$ is zero-dimensional if it has a base consisting of clopen sets.

Question: Does there exist a zero-dimensional (separable metrizable) topological space $X$ such that $X$ is not countable dense homogeneous, while the square $X^2 = X \times X$ is countable dense homogeneous? If so, can such an $X$ additionally be chosen to be rigid?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (2024–2025) has resolved the converse direction by constructing a zero-dimensional metrizable space that is CDH while its square is not CDH. The direction asked here — a non-CDH zero-dimensional space whose square is CDH, and the rigid version — does not appear to be answered in the literature available, and the problem still appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open problems on CDH, including questions about CDH behaviour under taking products and squares.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open problems on CDH.

status_evidence.title: Zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space X such that X^2 is not CDH
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a zero-dimensional metrizable CDH space whose square is not CDH, addressing the converse direction.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress addresses the converse direction (CDH with non-CDH square), not the direction asked here.
